message.content: The sea can appear in a wide range of colors depending on light, depth, and what's in the water. In clear, shallow tropical waters it often looks a brilliant turquoise or bright aqua. In deeper oceanic zones it shifts to deep blue or indigo. Near the coast, especially with sandy bottoms or algae, it can take on greenish or even golden hues. And under certain conditions—like sunrise, sunset, or when the water is full of plankton—the sea can glow with pinks, oranges, or reds. So, the “color” of the sea is really a spectrum that changes with time, place, and conditions.
